editorial.headline: Processed-Meat Retail: Nationally Open, Not Registrable for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This retail activity spans specialised sales of processed meat products, open nationally to every business scale but barred from PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Processed-meat retail is a specialised shop activity, not a catch-all food-trading category. It covers the retail sale of a range of processed meat products—whether derived from beef, pork, poultry, lamb, rabbit, goat, camel, or other fresh meats. Sausages, meatballs and shredded meat products are named examples. The commercial centre of gravity is therefore the sale of meat that has already been processed, presented through a retail business.

The activity is open to enterprises at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. Nationally, it is also classified as TERBUKA for foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the national position does not impose a foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. That openness is grounded in Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and it applies to the retail activity described here rather than to an assumed wider chain of production, distribution or food service.

Bali requires a separate reading. A foreign investor cannot register this activity for PMA in Bali today. At the Besar scale, OSS assigns Low or Medium-Low risk across every scope of the activity. Bali’s province-wide, permanent moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities from PMA registration, so the national 100% foreign-ownership position does not create a registrable PMA route on the island.

That distinction is the decisive one for founders. The national framework says the activity is open; Bali’s operative position says it is blocked for PMA because of its risk classification. The relevant Bali restriction took effect under the moratorium of May 2026, recorded in the Governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. For an operator planning specialised retail sales of sausages, meatballs or shredded meat products, the activity’s scope remains clear—but its Bali PMA position is equally clear: blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to full foreign ownership does not mean registrable for PMA in Bali.
